rationale: The router explicitly registers singular user/activation under the admin prefix; the contract explicitly declares the plural route.
ShouldBindJSON explicitly checks application/json and decodes filters; the operation explicitly lists two streaming request media types.
Retry exhaustion explicitly raises CONFLICT, mapped to 409. The deletion response list is silent about 409 rather than explicitly excluding it.
Malformed URL handling calls Error, whose body writer never sets an HTTP status. The operation explicitly describes verification and lists success and unauthorized statuses.
The invoice-error branch lacks a return before ResponseOk; both helpers serialize responses. The operation selects one Response object schema.

⚠️ Renamed fields have mappings only fromModel, with no inverse mapping on toModel. Missing reverse mappings explain lost input; dedicated property descriptions specify each field's meaning. Generated mapper code is absent.
An explicit length guard produces invalid_request, with configured default 4000. Unlimited length is inferred from the shared request schema's missing maxLength.

Verification examines references in the supplied context; deletion passes only assetId. The owner-context check is missing, while the operation summary explicitly scopes deletion to the given context.
The handler explicitly parses query filters and passes them to DeleteAllRelationTuples. The contract's lack of deletion parameters is silence.
The lookup's not-found translation reaches an explicit typed 500 response, whose writer sets 500. The operation explicitly lists 404 NotFound.
The handler is explicitly registered inside the admin group using AdminAuth. No-authentication is inferred from the absence of operation-level and root security declarations.
Unknown flags explicitly enter BlankResult, which initializes flagID to zero; the batch handler returns OK. Minimum 1 comes from the shared evalResult schema.
An explicit missing-parameter branch returns zero, and BuildTree explicitly replaces nonpositive depth with the configured limit. The operation explicitly requires max-depth.

The handler explicitly counts with includeSuppressed=true while getFindings explicitly filters suppressed entries. Both choices are visible; the operation separately promises all findings and a total header.

The mapper explicitly applies enabledEnrichers to the combined catalog, filtering both scopes. Dedicated prose distinguishes all flag-scoped entries from enabled built-ins, despite residing in a shared flag schema.
EnabledFlavors explicitly includes glob, and flavor checks that list. The deletion operation's parameter description explicitly names regex and exact.

Multipart processing explicitly constructs ScanUploadEvent, and its task explicitly invokes DependencyCheckParser. This targets scan processing structurally; possible copy-paste history is unavailable. Dedicated upload prose names CycloneDX and SPDX.
The batch handler reads and iterates only FlagIds; FlagKeys processing is omitted. The dedicated evaluationBatchRequest schema explicitly declares an array of nonempty flagKeys strings.

Unmarshal omits PurgeOnDelete although input conversion copies it. ⚠️ Preservation prose belongs to the separate /config operation; its applicability to the listing's shared configuration model is inferred.
The issuer-error branch explicitly calls ReplyStatusCode(500); that helper resets the response and sets text/plain plus a status message. The operation explicitly declares JSON for 500.
The resource explicitly constructs ClusteSummaryEntity and assigns clusterSummary. Its operation annotation explicitly selects ControllerStatusEntity, whose property is controllerStatus.
The resource explicitly declares @GET at commandtypes. The contract explicitly declares post at that path.
An explicit unknown-flag branch returns BlankResult with zero flagID, and the handler constructs OK. Minimum 1 is inherited from the shared evalResult schema.
The router explicitly binds GET under singular org and names its parameter keyName. The contract explicitly locates the operation under plural orgs with keyID.
Two explicit registrations assign listing to /fs/mem and file retrieval to /fs/mem/*. The contract explicitly declares a slash-suffixed listing route.
DELETE tag is explicitly placed in the authenticated router group. The contract contains no security declaration; its apparent unrestricted access follows from silence.
The parser accepts empty namespace and persistence explicitly adds a namespace predicate only when nonempty. Dedicated operation prose and required:true specify that namespace is mandatory.
The implementation explicitly names and reads hash. The operation explicitly declares its required hash-valued path parameter with the name thumb.
Unknown process IDs produce an error consumed by the handler's explicit 400 response construction. The update operation explicitly lists 404.
An explicit pre-dispatch decode catch writes invalid_request, mapped to 400. The listed auth/me responses omit 400 without an explicit exclusion rule.

GetInterface calls the configuration service and returns its result without body binding or validation. Required-body enforcement is omitted; the operation explicitly requires data with AddCommentReq.

The list mapper explicitly applies the enabled filter to combined built-in and flag-scoped enrichers. Dedicated catalog prose includes flag-scoped entries while qualifying only server built-ins as enabled.
The persistence path explicitly executes setParent(null) in its else branch. The POST operation explicitly says omitted or null parent leaves the existing parent unchanged.
The resource explicitly returns a referencing-components entity. The operation annotation explicitly selects ControllerServiceEntity as its response envelope.
Search returns a []Label collection, explicitly passed to c.JSON. The operation's successful response selects one search.Label object rather than an array wrapper.
The POST success branch logs and returns the user but omits a session userId assignment. The contract explicitly describes creating a new Session.
Persistence explicitly treats empty object and relation as absent filters. Their parameter entries require both, although contract prose contradictorily says only namespace is required.

Filtering leaves a nil Policies slice when nothing matches and forwards it to the writer. ⚠️ JSON null follows normal nil-slice serialization; writer internals are absent. The operation explicitly describes an array.
The GET method explicitly returns Collection<User>. The operation's successful response explicitly selects an array whose items reference Position.

Deletion uses ConstraintID without a flag or segment membership predicate. FlagID supplies snapshot metadata, and the transaction helper adds no ownership check. The operation explicitly requires flagID in its nested path.
Output conversion omits PurgeOnDelete, leaving false. ⚠️ Preservation prose is on /config; applying that promise to this operation's shared configuration model is an inference.
Segment deletion is keyed only by segmentID; required flagID supplies snapshot metadata without constraining membership. The operation explicitly nests the mutation beneath flagID.

The DAO and manager omit result pagination and return the whole matching list. The contract's page-selection promise comes from the reusable PaginatedApi annotation rather than dedicated endpoint prose.
The implementation explicitly wraps identifiers in apiAllKeys with JSON property keys. The operation explicitly describes and declares an array of key IDs.

The visible authorization callback checks the context, affected components, and controller services but omits inherited-context read checks. Dedicated security requirements explicitly name current and new inherited contexts; downstream implementations are not supplied.
HEAD uses VerifyGet; malformed URL handling calls Error, whose body writer never sets status. The operation explicitly lists successful verification and unauthorized responses.
The router explicitly assigns listing to /fs/disk and file retrieval to /fs/disk/*. The contract explicitly declares the listing path with its trailing slash.

The handler loses presence information by copying false into a struct field; vendored GORM explicitly skips blank false fields. This is an unaddressed framework interaction, despite dedicated enabled-filter prose.
The handler explicitly returns a view name, and the configured resolver explicitly emits text/html. The mapping explicitly declares text/plain; actual response resolution remains a static inference.
The router explicitly registers DELETE under singular org with keyName. The contract explicitly places the operation under plural orgs with keyID.

⚠️ PATCH merges into the DTO and invokes toModel, but renamed-field mappings exist only fromModel. Missing reverse mappings explain non-transfer; property descriptions are explicit. Generated mapper code is absent.
Position explicitly exposes a Network bean, whose getters define structured properties. The string requirement is inherited from the shared Position schema rather than dedicated operation prose.
An explicit message-length check returns invalid_request with default limit 4000. No maximum is stated in the shared ChatMessageRequest schema; that part of the contract claim derives from silence.
The router explicitly requires :member and the handler explicitly reads it. The contract locates deletion at the collection path and defines members in the removal request body.
The JSON builder explicitly writes query_time, record_count, page_size, and labels. The operation's response schema explicitly names took, total, num, and field.

The filter's result slice remains nil when no roles match and is passed to the response writer. ⚠️ Normal nil-slice JSON encoding yields null; writer internals are absent. The operation explicitly describes an array.
The route report explicitly returns Positions whose network property is a Network bean. The string constraint comes from the shared Position schema.
The handler explicitly serializes Album.Links(), a slice initialized as an empty collection. The successful operation response explicitly selects one entity.Link object.
The image lookup's not-found translation enters an explicit typed 500 response; its generated writer sets 500. The operation explicitly declares 404 NotFound.
Policy deletion uses flavor(), which explicitly accepts the EnabledFlavors list including glob. Its contract parameter prose explicitly names regex and exact.
The resource explicitly constructs ListingRequestEntity and assigns listingRequest after deletion. The operation explicitly documents DropRequestEntity as its response.
